answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity in something real: every agent stakes scarce compute or reputation before it votes or earns. Like a tide revealing what lies underwater, attestations from established peers wash away freshly minted fake accounts, while a raven carrying messages between nodes learns which perches return honest signatures. Root trust behaves like a willow: flexible under load, anchored deep, so an attacker must grow genuine history before gaining influence. Cheap mass sign-ups gain nothing; only verifiable participation compounds.
